days.title: AI-First OS Concepts: Current Research Map
days.learning: Keep model proposals behind deterministic enforcement of identity, authority, resources, and effects.
days.comparison: Cells, capabilities, and memory tiers exist. The external-call runtime bypasses its declared side-effect restriction.
days.acceptance: Deny an unauthorized external handler before invocation; preserve authorized execution and an audit trace.

days.title: AI-First OS Research Brief
days.learning: Convert repeated successful workflows into reusable, validated artifacts with explicit promotion and rollback.
days.comparison: The baseline imports bounded binary bundles but does not validate strings, ports, or graph structure. Day 2 adds validation before library registration.
days.acceptance: Reject malformed workflow artifacts before registration; exercise a valid packaged workflow in the guest.

days.title: AI-First OS Exploration: Control Planes, Kernels, and Scheduling
days.learning: Govern the scarce resources of an agent task, including tools, tokens, memory, and permissions.
days.comparison: The baseline reserves engine memory but ignores model-request deadlines and output limits. Day 3 enforces request admission and forwards cell limits.
days.acceptance: Exercise admission and release under bounded resources; reject work that exceeds its declared budget.

days.title: AI-First OS Research Update: Agentic Control Planes + AI-Tuned Scheduling
days.learning: Profile workloads before generating policies, then compare candidates against a fixed incumbent.
days.comparison: The baseline promotion gate can overflow score margins and thresholds. It does not resolve the declared incumbent. Day 4 widens arithmetic and checks incumbent installation.
days.acceptance: Reject a candidate indistinguishable from the incumbent and preserve the incumbent after rejection.

days.title: AI-First OS Exploration: Agent-Native Scheduling and Tunable Kernels
days.learning: Package observation, benchmarking, policy promotion, and rollback as auditable workflows.
days.comparison: The baseline has workflow execution and a capability promotion gate but no connection between them. Day 5 adds a permission-gated workflow step with sealed evidence and retained decisions.
days.acceptance: Execute an optimization workflow with explicit evidence and retain the prior policy after a failed gate.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Agent libOS + Tool-Call-Aware Resource Control
days.learning: Give tool calls their own resource scope within an agent lifecycle.
days.comparison: The baseline ignores recursion permission, configured child limits, cognitive inheritance, and slot cleanup. Day 6 enforces scoped derivation and ancestry admission, then returns slots on child destruction.
days.acceptance: Check that a child tool call cannot exceed its parent scope and releases resources on failure.

days.title: AI-First OS Exploration: Agent libOS + Tool-Call Scheduling
days.learning: Schedule and account for the tool invocation, where short resource spikes occur.
days.comparison: The baseline drops the materialized trace identifier and has no per-tool timing or byte accounting. Day 7 records those values and tests child slot ownership and release.
days.acceptance: Record per-tool timing, byte counts and outcomes; verify child slot acquisition and release through failure and success.

days.title: AI-First OS Exploration: Agent Runtime Meets Kernel Resource Control
days.learning: Separate agent identity, task branches, tool calls, and transport primitives.
days.comparison: The baseline omits parent and plan identifiers and leaves trace payloads writable. Day 8 preserves those identifiers and seals materialized traces.
days.acceptance: Exercise a child call through the runtime while preserving lineage and enforcing delegated authority.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Policy Enforcement Becomes the Control Plane
days.learning: Enforce policy beneath model-visible tools, where an action actually reaches the system.
days.comparison: The baseline treats object creator identity as caller authority. Day 9 supplies the active cell identity and enforces separate read and write handle permissions.
days.acceptance: Attempt a prohibited operation through the ordinary dispatch path and establish that no effect occurs.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Enforcement, Not Autonomy, Is Becoming the Core
days.learning: Admission, cancellation, and reaping belong to the runtime, alongside resource scheduling.
days.comparison: The baseline leaves descendants and duplicate queue entries after cancellation. Day 10 cancels queue ownership, preserves terminal runs, and reaps eligible child tasks.
days.acceptance: Cancel queued work and establish that no runnable entry or resource owner survives cancellation.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Stack Is Converging Around Enforcement
days.learning: Treat memory as a governed resource alongside agent execution and tool admission.
days.comparison: The baseline admits memory entries without a cell byte ceiling. Day 11 checks sealed payload admission against an inherited limit and retains its accounting owner until forgetting.
days.acceptance: Reject excessive admission while preserving an existing cell's usable memory.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Control Plane Is Becoming Concrete
days.learning: Make lifecycle and resource enforcement observable through one typed execution boundary.
days.comparison: The baseline permits external calls without saved traces and records generic denials. Day 12 reserves audit objects, records typed gates, and reports audit failure separately from completed execution.
days.acceptance: Produce a denial trace that identifies the failed gate and records no successful external effect.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Kernel Tunability + Policy-as-Code
days.learning: Represent tunable policy as a typed artifact with bounded revision authority.
days.comparison: The baseline accepts negative scoring divisors and unchecked weights or snapshots. Day 13 validates policy and snapshot bounds before simulation, preserving the previous result on rejection.
days.acceptance: Reject malformed simulation inputs without changing the previous result. A valid alternate candidate changes the simulated winner while replaying the incumbent reproduces its original result. Live policy activation remains outside this step.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Observability Is Becoming the Missing Plane
days.learning: Connect agent intent to the system effects and resource changes it caused.
days.comparison: The baseline retains caller identifiers and outcomes but uses a generic creation event. Day 14 preserves the intent name before dispatch or cancellation and verifies causal records after cell destruction.
days.acceptance: Trace an allowed effect and a denied effect back to separate requesting cells.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Scheduling Moves Above the Request Boundary
days.learning: Place sessions using continuity and locality, while different control loops run at appropriate timescales.
days.comparison: The baseline scores each route independently. Day 15 adds an optional session planner that retains eligible affinity, rechecks a declared backend pool, and preserves prior state on rejection.
days.acceptance: Preserve an eligible session's engine affinity while rejecting an unavailable engine.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Tool Calls and Inference Gangs Become Kernel Objects
days.learning: Mediate tool calls as governed operations and change inference resources only at safe boundaries.
days.comparison: The baseline checks authority only at effect preparation. Day 16 rechecks owner identity, lifecycle, permission, and data policy before dispatch while preserving settlement after dispatch begins.
days.acceptance: Reject revoked authority and changed data policy before dispatch. Preserve the prepared phase on rejection and permit outcome settlement after dispatch begins.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Context Becomes a Protected, Schedulable Resource
days.learning: Protect model-visible context by trust, version, scope, and residency.
days.comparison: The baseline bypasses metadata access policies in ICM. Day 17 enforces metadata permissions for views, catalogs, tags, and publication while keeping annotations separate from access authority.
days.acceptance: Deny unauthorized ICM projection and mutation. A public authority annotation must not grant access to protected metadata or payload, and authorized sealed-object annotations must remain usable.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Add a Slow Kernel-Configuration Loop
days.learning: Separate build configuration, runtime policy, and scheduler dispatch into distinct optimization loops.
days.comparison: The baseline records image hashes without a compiled configuration profile. Day 18 binds architecture and research mode to an artifact digest and checks the running guest.
days.acceptance: Bind the compiled architecture and research mode to the tested image; reject incompatible requirements and changed artifacts.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Separate the Immutable Authority Kernel from the Self-Evolving Capability Plane
days.learning: Allow capabilities to evolve while keeping their authority ceiling under independent control.
days.comparison: The baseline checks lifecycle and promotion scores without an independent authority ceiling. Day 19 checks private grants, installed lineage scope, and the promoting cell before registration.
days.acceptance: Reject ungranted or expanded execution authority; accept a scored replacement within the incumbent scope and the caller permissions.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Semantic Memory Metadata Is Becoming a Scheduling ABI
days.learning: Export semantic retention hints while the memory subsystem owns physical placement.
days.comparison: The baseline has tier records and decay without bounded hints or protected eviction. Day 20 ranks a bounded candidate pool while preserving controller-protected tiers.
days.acceptance: Exercise expiring retention advice and controlled tier eviction; preserve protected object content and reject unauthorized protection changes.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Semantic Control Loops Are Moving from Theory to Working Systems
days.learning: Use typed actions in slower control loops; retain deterministic resource ownership.
days.comparison: The baseline validates simulated weights but hardcodes live scoring. Day 21 activates typed, serialized policy trials and restores the prior weights after rejection.
days.acceptance: Reject malformed or stale tuning actions; observe live placement changes and restore the previous policy after a failed trial.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Identity Becomes a Signed Lifecycle Boundary
days.learning: Keep persistent agent identity separate from model, process, and host identity.
days.comparison: Baseline 4d6e43c has cell permissions and capability grants but no signed identity commitment. Day 022 adds signed authority history and admission across cell replacement.
days.acceptance: Require a valid operator signature for authority changes; preserve revocation across replacement cells and identify the admission commitment in traces.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The GUI Becomes a Semantic I/O Subsystem
days.learning: Expose graphical controls as typed objects with state and verifiable actions.
days.comparison: Baseline f0e4f56 has accessibility nodes but no observation generation or caller check. Day 023 adds authorized focus with stale-target rejection and a verified focus receipt.
days.acceptance: Reject stale or unauthorized control actions and verify that an allowed focus action reaches the intended surface.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: “Pause” Must Be an Effect Fence
days.learning: A pause must fence effects across the relevant execution scope.
days.comparison: Baseline 2b8df85 checks individual cell authority but lacks a shared run fence. Day 024 adds inherited holds, sticky terminal epochs, and governed dispatch checks.
days.acceptance: Hold one branch and block sibling effects in the same run while harmless computation and unrelated runs can continue.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Tool Catalogs Become a Virtual I/O Namespace
days.learning: Expose a bounded tool namespace through capability handles instead of loading every schema into context.
days.comparison: Baseline 5111209 has capability records and a transport registry but no scoped catalog or revocable tool handle. Day 025 adds bounded discovery and current-grant invocation checks.
days.acceptance: Bound discovery to authorized entries and reject invocation through revoked, stale, foreign, or altered tool handles.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Schedule Continuity, Not Isolated Requests
days.learning: Schedule continuation state using dependencies, residency, and expected reuse.
days.comparison: Baseline 654d3e8 retains eligible session affinity indefinitely. Day 026 adds expiring, cost-aware reuse of validated logical state while preserving current engine permission checks.
days.acceptance: Prefer readable, validated resident state only while the hint remains useful and unexpired, without selecting an ineligible engine.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Skills Become Schedulable Behavioral Packages
days.learning: Treat skills as versioned behavioral packages with dependencies, permissions, and evaluations.
days.comparison: The prior validator accepted a missing required engine at score 75. Validation and installation now require bounded, unique dependencies with current readiness; the existing authority ceiling also applies.
days.acceptance: Reject a behavioral package with unsatisfied dependencies or a wider permission request.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Agent Trajectories Become Security and Scheduling Objects
days.learning: Authorize trajectories using accumulated lineage and effects, rather than isolated calls alone.
days.comparison: The baseline checked declared object labels but forgot sensitive reads across calls. Bound run fences now retain the highest read sensitivity and constrain later protected effects across branches.
days.acceptance: Deny a prohibited sequence even when its individual operations are separately available.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Causal Control and DAG-Aware Caching
days.learning: Preserve workflow intermediates according to causal importance and reconstruction cost.
days.comparison: The baseline could evict produced inputs needed by unfinished workflow nodes. Eviction, demotion, and forgetting now preserve those inputs across active and paused workflows until their consumers finish.
days.acceptance: Retain an intermediate needed by runnable descendants and reclaim one with no live consumer.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Target Knowledge Becomes an Optimization Artifact
days.learning: Make target knowledge and task state explicit, versioned inputs to optimization.
days.comparison: The baseline bound tuning actions to policy generations only. Optional target contracts and sealed proposal artifacts now recheck the compiled profile, selected engine settings, and versioned knowledge and evaluation references.
days.acceptance: Reject an optimization artifact whose target description no longer matches the tested environment.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Harness Becomes the Optimization Kernel
days.learning: Trust the evaluation harness to establish correctness and measurement, independently of the generating agent.
days.comparison: The baseline accepted caller-authored evaluation payloads after checking target compatibility. Artifact trials now require an issued passing receipt from fixed routing checks, bound to the complete candidate action.
days.acceptance: Reject missing or mismatched evidence and accept only an independently checked candidate.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Execution Scope and Loop Governance Become OS Primitives
days.learning: Grant bounded execution leases and enlarge them only through an explicit decision.
days.comparison: The baseline bounds concurrent children but returns slots after destruction. Day 32 adds a shared lifetime creation budget, explicit expansion, and permanent lease expiry.
days.acceptance: Reject a child beyond the shared lifetime budget without allocation; permit explicit expansion and fence new children and effects after expiry.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Typed Kernel Policy and Explicit Revision Authority
days.learning: Compile policy and its boundary contracts together; distinguish parameter changes from authority changes.
days.comparison: The baseline has no revision grant between active-cell denial of tuning and permission to install capabilities. Day 33 adds parameter and implementation ceilings, inherited leases, and trial ownership.
days.acceptance: Permit bounded parameter trials under an inherited grant while rejecting implementation changes, authority expansion, foreign trial acceptance, and revoked grants.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Separate Speculative Execution from Verified Authority
days.learning: Speculate about resource preparation while withholding authority for durable effects.
days.comparison: The baseline stages writes but permits publication without current effect authority or actor checks. Day 34 gates publication and shadow writes while preserving explicit abort.
days.acceptance: Reject staged publication without effect permission or during a hold; abort preserves committed state and prevents external dispatch.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Semantic Data Movement and Proof-Carrying Scheduling
days.learning: Describe data movement semantically and validate the implementation's scheduling invariants.
days.comparison: The baseline matches raw prefixes and skips policy checks at write and commit. Day 35 validates namespace boundaries, rejects truncation, and rechecks destination policy while preserving digest continuity.
days.acceptance: Reject invalid or revoked destinations before more bytes or a committed result; preserve the exact digest across interruption and resume.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Federated Scheduling and Admission Contracts
days.learning: Delegate bounded scheduling authority to domains and distinguish reservation from readiness.
days.comparison: The baseline accounts for flat global leases. Day 36 adds bounded parent grants, shared root accounting, and subtree revocation with explicit record cleanup.
days.acceptance: Reject a child beyond its parent grant; preserve global accounting across nesting and restore ledger capacity after quiescent subtree revocation.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Agent Graph Becomes a Schedulable Resource
days.learning: Treat the agent graph as versioned execution state with bounded structural changes.
days.comparison: The baseline executes workflow graphs but lacks controlled topology revisions. The candidate validates complete edge replacements against frozen nodes, requires sealed evidence from the current revision, and adds bounded rollback.
days.acceptance: Reject invalid graph revisions without changing the runnable original; execute the revised and restored orders; deny stale, over-budget, and paused changes.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Agent Runtime Needs a JIT
days.learning: Compile repeated trajectories into deterministic or hybrid workflows and demote them when conditions change.
days.comparison: The baseline validates templates but does not pin reuse assumptions. The candidate binds hybrid or deterministic forms to graph and object digests, reevaluates read access, and demotes stale or failed forms before reuse.
days.acceptance: Run a deterministic state-to-output artifact, then reject changed or deleted preconditions before dispatch; check graph drift, read revocation, and sticky failure demotion.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Continuation State Becomes the New Process Image
days.learning: Represent a continuation across semantic history, tokens, model state, tools, and device placement.
days.comparison: The baseline keeps progress in memory but only serializes graph text. The candidate seals and unloads a bounded continuation image, checks its graph and dependencies on restore, and prevents replay of a consumed checkpoint.
days.acceptance: Restore unloaded workflow progress and retain the completed result object without repeating its creation; reject drift, revoked access, and checkpoint replay.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Compile Intent into Control Policy
days.learning: Compile natural-language intent into typed objectives and constraints before searching policy candidates.
days.comparison: The baseline validates weights and evidence but has no typed policy task. The candidate checks declared domains and units, evaluates fixed observable constraints, and binds the complete task to required passing receipts.
days.acceptance: Reject infeasible typed bounds before evaluation or activation; deny failing or mismatched evidence; admit and roll back a passing compiled task.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Observation Coherence and Semantic I/O Scheduling
days.learning: Schedule observations by validity, provenance, cost, and supersession.
days.comparison: Object metadata and interface structure now feed a bounded observation catalog. Reads reject changed, missing, inaccessible, and superseded dependencies; historical bytes remain accessible under normal policy. An interrupt regression also fixes unsafe x86 compiler stack use.
days.acceptance: Reject an observation superseded by a newer state transition.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Schedule Agent Roles and Phase Transitions
days.learning: Schedule agent roles and workflow phases instead of treating an entire campaign as one request.
days.comparison: Engine leases now support controller-issued role contracts and one active phase per cell. Busy reservations block transitions; stale or excessive requests cannot replace the current lease. Cell lifetime remains pinned until phase closure and detachment.
days.acceptance: Release a finished phase's lease before starting a phase with different resource needs.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Semantic Transactions + Workload Compilation
days.learning: Preserve a workflow's semantic environment across suspension and compile repeated work where valid.
days.comparison: A sealed semantic manifest now pins named artifact versions, compatibility declarations, schemas, and the workflow graph. Start, resume, save, and restore check the manifest before changing execution state; mismatches preserve the continuation and permit abort.
days.acceptance: Reject resume against changed semantic dependencies and preserve the original continuation.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Treat Kernel Tuning as Profile Synthesis, Not Runtime Autonomy
days.learning: Synthesize kernel profiles offline and select validated profiles deterministically at runtime.
days.comparison: A trusted compiler now seals finite routing cases and measured simulation results against a captured incumbent and engine environment. The live planner selects the issued profile per decision only while that envelope matches; all rejections retain incumbent weights.
days.acceptance: Reject a profile outside its validated operating envelope and use the incumbent.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Speculation Becomes a First-Class OS Primitive
days.learning: Prepare predicted futures cheaply and commit only after deterministic validation.
days.comparison: A bounded speculation broker now keeps candidate object replacements private. Publication requires matching action bytes, origin state, deadline, and current staged-write authority. Incorrect, stale, expired, or unauthorized candidates close without publishing their payload or dispatching an external handler.
days.acceptance: Discard an incorrect prediction without changing committed state or invoking a handler.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The AI Scheduler Is Becoming a Policy Compiler
days.learning: Use AI as a policy compiler while a deterministic controller builds, measures, and accepts candidates.
days.comparison: Compiled source fingerprints now bind kernel and UEFI artifacts, guest regressions, and host records before a candidate receives a validation record.
days.acceptance: Reject absent, contradictory, or mismatched image validation; accept the matching source candidate after both VM modes pass the complete regression range.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Push the Policy Foundry Below the Kernel
days.learning: Apply bounded search to hardware policy while respecting physical capacity.
days.comparison: The native profile compiler now calculates storage and work requirements and rejects declared budgets before allocation or evaluation.
days.acceptance: Reject insufficient artifact, scratch, or simulation budgets without publishing a profile; use an exact-budget candidate after ordinary validation.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Make the Agent Working Set Semantic
days.learning: Manage the semantic working set by readiness, utility, reconstruction cost, provenance, and dependencies.
days.comparison: Semantic manifests now protect declared live dependencies and pin controller-issued memory validation generations before reuse or resume.
days.acceptance: Keep paused dependency chains resident, reject contested or revalidated evidence under the old manifest, and recover through explicit rebinding.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Separate Advice from Ownership
days.learning: Let AI supply advice while deterministic subsystems retain ownership of placement, eviction, and commit.
days.comparison: Direct placement is now controller-only, owner cleanup preserves admission accounting, and L4 promotion accepts only provisional or validated state.
days.acceptance: Verify maximum hints cannot override placement authority or memory ceilings, while owners can release charges after permission revocation.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Virtualize Semantic Liveness, Not Just Memory
days.learning: Separate logical liveness from physical allocation so dead state does not pin an entire allocation.
days.comparison: Bounded logical views now preserve record identity and aliases while verified compaction reclaims native physical pages.
days.acceptance: Reclaim dead records from fragmented pages while surviving aliases retain identical bytes and identity; preserve mappings after rejected copies.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Decouple the Scaling Unit from the Agent
days.learning: Use different units for identity, isolation, scaling, scheduling, and failure.
days.comparison: Controllers can resize active phase reservations while retaining task and lease identity. Contract ceilings, shared capacity, recorded usage, and child reservations constrain each change.
days.acceptance: Grow and shrink one phase without changing task identity; reject stale requests, overcommitment, and unsafe shrinkage.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Capacity Should Be Leased Just in Time
days.learning: Separate resource entitlement from current ownership and allocate physical capacity near use.
days.comparison: A controller can park an active phase, releasing its reservation while preserving its private entitlement. Reactivation competes for current capacity and retains task identity.
days.acceptance: Release idle reservations, reject reacquisition under competing demand, and restore the saved request after capacity becomes available.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Determinism Should Be a Schedulable Resource
days.learning: Declare consistency requirements explicitly and stage effects when stronger guarantees need them.
days.comparison: Runtime admission now rejects semantic, transactional, token-stable, and automatically staged contracts that lack enforcement. Explicit single-object staging retains visibility, conflict, and abort checks.
days.acceptance: Reject unsupported contracts before handlers run; verify explicit staged visibility, conflict rejection, abort provenance, and successful publication.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Model Updates Need Transaction Semantics
days.learning: Publish model adaptations atomically and key caches by the served model version.
days.comparison: Anxml can stage and test private toy adapters before publishing their serving generation and cache identity together. Rollback restores the prior image under a fresh generation.
days.acceptance: Keep the old adapter serving until verified publication; check changed tokens, stale cache rejection, unrelated adapter isolation, and rollback.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Runtime Boundary Is Becoming an Authority Kernel
days.learning: Check operation authority, information flow, resource admission, and outcome evidence independently.
days.comparison: Direct calls now enforce fenced-run sensitivity. Explicit protected operations bind copied requests to destinations and retain ambiguous provider outcomes without redispatching the same identifier.
days.acceptance: Deny confidential egress without destination permission; verify approved dispatch, source and provider rechecks, and retained UNKNOWN outcomes that block redispatch.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Build a Resource Digital Twin Before a Learned Scheduler
days.learning: Use a bounded resource model to compare near-term scheduling choices before changing the live system.
days.comparison: The Twin now checks declared restoration demand against frozen logical capacity. Live admission still rechecks reservations before use.
days.acceptance: Compare frozen and live routing, then prove memory and accelerator contention can invalidate restoration feasibility.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: AI Should Be the Regime-Change Controller, Not the Default Scheduler
days.learning: Invoke adaptation when deterministic telemetry detects a departure from the validated regime.
days.comparison: Bound regions now retain calibrated limits across sustained drift and emit one investigation event per exit. Events grant no policy authority.
days.acceptance: Exercise stationary telemetry, sustained and repeated departures, stale events, rejected tuning, and return to the calibrated range.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Schedule the Cognitive Plan Before the Hardware
days.learning: Budget model choice, reasoning, skills, and context before physical placement.
days.comparison: Native Anxml now applies captured per-generation ceilings, including workflow and adapter calls. Effective ceilings also participate in adapter cache identity.
days.acceptance: Run bounded workflow inference, direct and adapter generation, nested ceilings, prompt access denials, cancellation, and stale cache checks.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Late Binding May Be the Core Model-Native OS Abstraction
days.learning: Keep logical identity stable while binding physical representation and execution late.
days.comparison: Private model bindings now capture logical declarations and object versions, then recheck readiness and policy before changing engines. Backend equivalence remains a controller claim.
days.acceptance: Preserve Cell and model identity across local engine changes; reject stale inputs, unavailable servers, revoked leases, and unauthorized placement.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Build a Model-State Fabric, Not Just a Model Scheduler
days.learning: Treat model state as a movable resource with identity, validity, and transfer costs.
days.comparison: Immutable resource views now move between pools with the same owner. All aliases retain identity, copied bytes are verified before publication, and adapter consumers still reject stale derivation keys.
days.acceptance: Move executable adapter state across physical pools; preserve aliases and owner access, reject failed copies, and invalidate stale model generations.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Linux 7.3 Makes Hierarchical Scheduling a Real Kernel Primitive
days.learning: Delegate revocable CPU ownership through a scheduler hierarchy.
days.comparison: Private scheduler domains now bound bootstrap-CPU eligibility, queue classes, priority, and expiry through a Cell hierarchy. Revocation blocks descendants at dequeue and runtime admission; enforcement remains cooperative.
days.acceptance: Revoke a child domain and deny its queued and direct descendant work; run a healthy sibling and reject tool dispatch after live expiry.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Reasoning Itself Is Becoming a Schedulable Parallel Program
days.learning: Distinguish required parallel subtasks from competing trials in the execution graph.
days.comparison: Native branch groups now distinguish required results from competing trials. They execute bounded toy-model candidates as pure child Cells, verify exact outputs, preserve parent fences, and expose only completed-group results.
days.acceptance: Accept a verified trial winner and cancel unstarted alternatives. Require every AND result, enforce the shared budget, and deny branch effects.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Harness Is Becoming a JIT-Compiled Control Image
days.learning: Treat a generated harness as a bounded control program validated against a stable interface.
days.comparison: Baseline 0bf1fce has workflows and verified model groups. This step adds a bounded control-image ABI, validation, private authority grants, and execution with immutable event history.
days.acceptance: Reject malformed images and stale epochs before execution. Recover from one failed model group, return the verified second result, and preserve both outcomes.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Trust Has to Survive from Intent to Physical Use
days.learning: Bind intent, delegation, effects, and the bytes used at execution time into one causal chain.
days.comparison: Baseline 4ae6479 validates source dependencies but has no prepared inference receipt. This step binds sources and identity, verifies the CPU execution copy, and records consumed-image evidence.
days.acceptance: Reject changed sources, identity commitments, and corrupted execution copies. Execute fresh records and verify their source, consumed-image, and output digests.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Optimize Execution Shape Before Scheduling It
days.learning: Optimize execution shape before placement and measure the complete workflow.
days.comparison: Baseline 2a46190 has prepared inference records. This step compiles bounded reuse plans, preserves dependency and authority boundaries, and completes equivalent logical outputs with fewer CPU generations.
days.acceptance: Match all logical outputs while reducing completed CPU generations from three to two. Preserve dependency and authority boundaries and reject stale plans.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Compile Experience into Versioned Procedural Artifacts
days.learning: Compile experience into versioned procedural artifacts with traceable evidence.
days.comparison: ICM and provenance classify stored artifacts; verified model-use receipts identify actual computation. The procedure registry now preserves source evidence, binds exact dependencies, and requires a separate replay before execution.
days.acceptance: Reject missing evidence, changed dependencies, incompatible requests, and forged catalog grants. Require separate replays and execute both recipe versions without widening permissions.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Agent Runtime Should Be a Process Graph, Not a Monolithic Harness
days.learning: Keep durable continuation identity while composing replaceable execution processes.
days.comparison: Workflow checkpoints and protected operations exist. The continuation registry now retains a logical owner, versioned worker bindings, sealed results, and duplicate-call protection across worker replacement.
days.acceptance: Replace workers after completion or failure. Preserve the logical owner and recorded result; block duplicate keys, stale bindings, changed evidence, and foreign access.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Suspension Needs to Become a First-Class OS State
days.learning: Distinguish long suspension from short I/O waits and reclaim expensive idle state.
days.comparison: Day 067 retains semantic continuation records, and Day 052 parks phase leases. Day 068 coordinates short waits, long suspensions, and physical model-cache reclamation with guarded reconstruction.
days.acceptance: Preserve completions through suspension, reclaim the model cache, reject invalid restoration, and execute the reconstructed image.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Resume from a Frontier, Not from a Fully Restored Image
days.learning: Resume from the minimum usable state frontier while restoring later dependencies incrementally.
days.comparison: Day 068 restores one continuation cache. Day 069 coordinates ordered model-image readiness, checks phase ownership, and executes from the next restored image.
days.acceptance: Execute from a ready frontier, reject missing or stale state, and preserve output equivalence with complete restoration.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Schedule Externalities, Not Just Resource Consumption
days.learning: Account for interference imposed on other workloads and exposure from external effects.
days.comparison: Protected operations preserve committed and uncertain outcomes. Day 070 reserves controller-assigned exposure across a shared hierarchy and keeps uncertain charges after revocation.
days.acceptance: Reject shared budget overdrafts before dispatch; preserve uncertain charges and distinguish revoked authority from unresolved operations.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Separate the Logical Program from the Physical Machine Plan
days.learning: Preserve an authoritative logical graph while deriving a replaceable physical execution plan.
days.comparison: Day 065 compiles and runs a complete execution shape. Day 071 separates immutable logical inputs from one-step physical plans bound to logical and resource epochs.
days.acceptance: Reject stale physical plans while preserving logical progress, then recompile a valid prefix and retain equivalent results.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Schedule Evidence and Intent, Not Just Compute
days.learning: Allocate independent evidence paths and durable future intentions alongside physical resources.
days.comparison: Staged writes now bind reviewer approvals to current evidence ancestry and enforce a minimum structural cut before ordinary commit.
days.acceptance: Reject shared and mixed evidence roots, exclude corrupted dependencies, and commit only with two surviving independent approvals.

days.title: AI-First OS Update: Make the Adaptive Kernel Proof-Carrying
days.learning: Attach independently checked evidence to adaptive policy and enforce context privilege monotonicity.
days.comparison: The context compiler binds source ancestry to role and scope ceilings. Existing policy gates check evidence rather than formal proofs.
days.acceptance: Reject role and scope escalation through summaries, stale ancestors, foreign access, and partial output on failed context assembly.

days.learning: Separate stable logical state from a versioned resource shape and recheck placement after reconfiguration.
days.comparison: Physical plans now capture a separate resource-shape epoch and consume private model replicas while preserving the logical program.
days.acceptance: Resize actual replica pages, reject stale shape and phase placements, and preserve completed results and logical identity.
days.title: AI-First OS Update: Make Resource Shape a Schedulable Object

days.learning: Give planners explicit execution constraints and versioned compatibility contracts for memory, models, coordination, and quality.
days.comparison: Memory indices bind reader and embedding descriptors to exact source snapshots and reject incompatible reuse after contract replacement.
days.acceptance: Reject equal-dimension space and reader replacements, rebuild from canonical evidence, and allow queries only under matching contracts.
days.title: AI-First OS Update: Define Semantic ABIs Between Models, Memory, Teams, and Hardware

days.learning: Expose logical memory objects and their consumers, then choose physical representations according to topology and measured benefit.
days.comparison: Resource shapes can now coalesce verified immutable replicas under an explicit access contract and a physical page-saving threshold.
days.acceptance: Reject incompatible or unprofitable sharing without changing copies; reduce two pages to one and preserve verified outputs through fresh plans.
days.title: AI-First OS Update: The Memory Scheduler Is Becoming as Important as the CPU Scheduler

days.learning: Control computation depth, speculation, and parallelism within explicit quality and resource limits, with deterministic enforcement.
days.comparison: Anunix records verified model execution. The new workload controller freezes output requirements, admits measured candidates, and enforces a selected token allowance.
days.acceptance: Reject candidates that violate the frozen prefix, length, or token bounds. Execute accepted eight-token and four-token choices with fresh receipts and unchanged quality requirements.
days.title: AI-first OS update — September 10: schedule the amount of computation, not only where it runs

days.learning: Use agent phases, idle intervals, lineage, and shared origins to schedule state movement while preserving capacity and correctness.
days.comparison: Continuation hibernation already preserves semantic state. Model waits now admit lineage-bound cache reclamation while retaining the existing phase reservation.
days.acceptance: Reclaim sibling caches only during current model waits, reject stale or incompatible requests, and restore verified CPU output without changing the retained reservation.
days.title: AI-first OS update — September 11: treat agent idle time and lineage as schedulable resources

days.learning: Bind scheduling decisions to execution phases and state versions, then revalidate those assumptions at commit.
days.comparison: Existing shape resizing validates a supplied shape epoch. The new decision also binds progress, phase capacity, resident geometry, identity, and run-fence generation across planning.
days.acceptance: Seven stale observations reject without changing resource geometry or caller output. A fresh private decision commits two replicas, preserves completed work, and completes both CPU operations.
days.title: AI-first OS update — September 12: schedule phases, progress, and state versions

days.learning: Treat speculation as a bounded transaction with isolated mutable state, buffered external effects, and explicit commit or abort.
days.comparison: Staged mutations, pending effects, and run fences exist. A shared speculation domain must coordinate state and external-effect admission.
days.acceptance: Abort a speculative branch without dispatching its buffered effects; admit only the validated branch at commit.
days.title: AI-first OS update — September 13: reversible execution is becoming a kernel primitive
AI-first OS update — September 14: compile intelligence into a closed policy space, then let AI select
days.learning: Keep runtime policy selection inside a previously validated, finite action space.
days.comparison: Finite routing profiles and typed tuning actions exist. A versioned policy catalog with indexed selection still needs an explicit runtime boundary.
days.acceptance: Select only issued policies through a bounded index; prove invalid or stale selections retain the validated fallback.

days.title: AI-first OS update — September 15: schedule the continuation, not the process
days.learning: Keep resource entitlement with a continuation while deterministic gates constrain handoffs, authority sources, and policy rules.
days.comparison: Cells, scheduler domains, and phase leases constrain individual execution. Shared continuation entitlement and explicit holder handoff need a common runtime boundary.
days.acceptance: Transfer a bounded continuation entitlement between authorized members without duplicating capacity. Reject foreign, stale, or revoked handoffs.
